description: Büyük başarılar, kesinlikten değil; başkalarının imkânsız gördüğü hedeflerin peşinden gitme cesaretinden doğar. Bilimsel araştırmayı, stratejik düşünceyi ve entelektüel disiplini birleştiren; ulusal ve uluslararası başarılarla yetkinliğini kanıtlamış bir ekibiz. Hedefimiz, Galactic Impact Ödülü'ne layık, özgün ve uygulanabilir bir çözüm geliştirmektir. Mükemmellik standardımızdır. Etki yaratmak ise amacımızdır.
summary: Falconia is a web prototype for exploring MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations through an interactive map, a burning-activity calendar and traceable source records. Because the sensors differ in spatial resolution, sensitivity and observation timing, more hotspots do not automatically mean more fires. Users can select an area and period, compare observations and inspect the records behind a pattern. The project connects satellite observations with contextual evidence to support clearer investigation of burning activity. The demonstration illustrates the workflow; full historical-data verification, independent sensor-calibration tests and a connected, source-based AI assistant remain development goals. Falconia is designed to help researchers, land managers and local analysts explore fire patterns while keeping uncertainty visible.
details:
WHAT WE BUILT

Falconia — Mapping Fire, Revealing Patterns is a browser-based prototype developed for the Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challenge. It brings an interactive map, a burning-activity calendar, sensor comparisons and source records into one workflow.

Users can select an area and date range, filter observations, inspect individual records and review when and where thermal activity was detected. The aim is to make patterns easier to investigate while keeping the observations behind them accessible.

THE PROBLEM

MODIS and VIIRS observe thermal activity at different spatial resolutions and times. Differences in sensitivity, coverage and satellite overpasses mean that their raw detection counts cannot be treated as interchangeable measurements of fire activity. More hotspots do not automatically mean more independent fires.

Falconia addresses this problem by making sensor differences and data limitations visible during exploration.

HOW IT WORKS

The prototype supports CSV and JSON observations, geographic and date filters, sensor comparisons and record-level inspection. Observations can be grouped into a common spatial grid and UTC days to support consistent exploration.

The calendar connects activity on a particular day with the underlying observations. Record details retain information such as the sensor, satellite platform, observation time, location and available source fields.

Users can attach contextual sources to possible explanations and export information for further review. Agricultural burning, industrial heat and other possible explanations remain hypotheses unless supported by independent evidence. Satellite hotspots alone do not establish ignition cause.

OUR APPROACH TO HARMONIZATION

Spatial and temporal alignment is a first step. Statistical correction of sensor differences is a separate task that requires verified overlapping observations, knowledge of observation coverage and independent evaluation.

We do not claim that placing MODIS and VIIRS observations on the same grid makes the sensors equivalent. The intended next stage is to evaluate sensor adjustment against unadjusted observations and test its performance on a separate period.

CURRENT STATUS

The demonstration uses sample observations to illustrate the interface and analysis workflow. These samples have not been independently verified against the original NASA source files and should not be interpreted as evidence of a historical trend or calibration accuracy.

Current summaries are rule-based. A connected AI assistant that explains results using traceable sources is planned as a later addition. Full historical-data integration and independent validation also remain development goals.

TOOLS AND NASA RESOURCES

The web prototype uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG, CSV and JSON, with Three.js for optional 3D visuals.

NASA FIRMS documentation informed the observation fields, sensor distinctions and interpretation limits. NASA GIBS supplies geographic background imagery, which is separate from the active-fire observations. The accompanying presentation uses credited NASA Earth Observatory archive imagery.

AI ASSISTANCE

ChatGPT assisted brainstorming, research synthesis, interface design, coding, troubleshooting, documentation, translation and presentation preparation. This development assistance is distinct from the planned AI assistant inside the application. AI-assisted code and design are disclosed in the supplied prototype.

INTENDED IMPACT

Researchers could use this workflow to investigate sensor disagreement. Land managers and local analysts could examine recurring burning periods and connect satellite observations with independent event records.

Our contribution is the connection between the map, calendar, sensor comparison and traceable evidence in one interface. The intended benefit is a clearer investigation process; no measured accuracy or environmental-impact percentage is claimed.

LIMITATIONS AND NEXT STEPS

A hotspot does not directly measure an independent fire, burned area or future fire spread. Missing observations do not establish that no fire occurred. Falconia is an exploratory prototype, not an emergency alert or evacuation system.

Next steps are to integrate verified historical observations, evaluate sensor adjustment independently, strengthen contextual evidence and add source-based AI explanations.
